top_story.headline: Rep. Joaquin Castro files West Bank and Gaza settlement sanctions bill in a three-minute House session
top_story.dek: The measure, H.R. 10642, was one of 98 introduced in a three-minute House session with no votes.
paragraphs: Among the 80 public bills introduced in the House on Thursday, October 1, 2026, the most politically charged is a sanctions measure on West Bank and Gaza settlements. It was sponsored by Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX-20) with more than 40 cosponsors listed in the Congressional Record, among them Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY-14), and was referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs with the Committees on the Judiciary, Financial Services, and Ways and Means added for consideration of their portions.

The bill, per the Record, would “provide for the imposition of sanctions with respect to settlements in the West Bank and Gaza, and for other purposes.” The text had not been analyzed for this edition; only the title and referral as printed in the Record were read.

The House held no votes. According to the Daily Digest, the chamber met at 11:30 a.m. and adjourned at 11:33 a.m. with no roll-call votes, no recorded votes and no quorum calls, and the Senate was in a 35-second pro forma session. Both chambers were scheduled to reconvene Monday, October 5, 2026.

sections.headline: Pro forma sessions in both chambers; 98 House measures introduced
paragraphs: Both chambers held brief pro forma sessions on Thursday, October 1, 2026. The House met from 11:30 a.m. to 11:33 a.m. with no recorded votes, no roll-call votes, and no quorum calls; the Senate met from 10:30:06 a.m. to 10:30:41 a.m. The House filed one committee report, on H.R. 6993, a bill on traumatic brain injury research grants through the Department of Veterans Affairs (House Report 119-838), and held two Senate bills, S. 3257 and S. 3258, at the desk. The Speaker also announced his signature on three Senate-passed enrolled bills on Tuesday, September 29: S. 240 (Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 improvements), S. 283 (a standard methodology for identifying the country of origin of seafood), and S. 2403 (a definition of adequate consideration for certain closely held stock under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974).

House members introduced 98 measures: 80 public bills (H.R. 10640–10719), one private bill (H.R. 10720), one joint resolution, one concurrent resolution, and 15 simple resolutions. Beyond the West Bank and Gaza sanctions bill, the most notable are a constitutional amendment to abolish the Electoral College from Rep. Steve Cohen, a Posse Comitatus Act bill from Rep. Patrick Ryan, and a rule resolution from Rep. Jason Crow to bring the Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026 to the floor. The complete list follows.
